title: Renewal Check-in — Capacity uplift & EU/APAC onramp
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in. BlueOak is approaching contract renewal window and wants to add baseline capacity, enable EU region, and pilot APAC bursting. Discussed latency targets, data residency, SOC2 audit timing, and pricing options for reserved + burst. SE offered benchmark plan and proposed timeline for EU onramp pilot next month.
topics: Current usage profile and tail latency
action_items: Maya Chen - Send revised pricing spreadsheet with 12/24 month term options and burst pricing - 2026-11-09
Diego Alvarez - Run 99th percentile latency benchmark on BlueOak sample workload and share results - 2026-11-06
Priya Raman - Share current traffic patterns, P95/P99 and token distribution CSV - 2026-11-04
BlueOak (Liam) - Confirm legal timeline and preferred contract term (12 vs 24 months) - 2026-11-10
next_steps: Redwood to deliver benchmark results and updated pricing
Schedule EU onramp pilot kickoff (2-week pilot) w/ infra owners
Customer to prepare traffic sample and security questionnaire answers
Follow-up call to align on PO and SOW after benchmarks
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Liam O'Rourke (BlueOak Head of MLOps), Priya Raman (BlueOak Platform Eng), Jules Martin (BlueOak CTO)

Summary (auto): Quarterly renewal + expansion discussion. Customer wants baseline uplift, EU region with private VPC, and short APAC pilot. Discussed tradeoffs on latency vs cost, reserved capacity sizing, SOC2 timing.

00:00:03 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into usage and renewal items.
00:00:12 - Liam O'Rourke: Hey Maya, thanks. Liam here, Priya and Jules are with me.
00:00:16 - Priya Raman: Hi all.
00:00:18 - Jules Martin: Hello.
00:00:21 - Diego Alvarez: Diego from Redwood, nice to meet you all.
00:00:24 - Maya Chen: Cool. So objective for today, we want to align on capacity uplift and EU region onramp and talk about APAC pilot. I'll hand it to Liam to give a quick status update on how things are trending on your side.

00:00:40 - Liam O'Rourke: Sure. So overall things look good, we're seeing steady growth — token volume up about 2.4x since July. Most traffic is US-east, but EU has been ramping with product localization. We currently have a reserved pool that covers baseline but bursts during end-of-month reports cause throttles. The renewal is due mid-December, so we're trying to lock in capacity and region plans ahead of time.
00:01:05 - Priya Raman: To add, we've had a few P99 spikes in the EU when we route to US by default; it's about 450-700ms at the tail which is problematic for certain product flows.
00:01:18 - Jules Martin: We're also concerned about data residency — legal wants logs kept in EU for EU customers and SOC2 evidence updated.
00:01:26 - Maya Chen: Got it. Thanks — that matches what we saw on the usage dashboard. Diego, can you walk through options for reserved vs burst and what a mixed model looks like?

00:01:40 - Diego Alvarez: Yeah. So typically for teams in this scenario we offer a baseline reserved capacity sized for steady-state throughput and then a burst pool or credits for spikes. For BlueOak's profile we recommend increasing baseline by ~40% and adding a burst bucket equivalent to another ~20% of current peak. That keeps steady latency low while allowing spikes without throttling. The math I used assumes similar batch sizes and a median sequence length of ~120 tokens from your sample.
00:02:10 - Liam O'Rourke: That 40% figure — is that just to cover forecasted traffic or do you factor in batching optimizations Redwood suggests?
00:02:18 - Diego Alvarez: We factored in current observed batching. There's room to reduce baseline needs by enabling prefix caching and slightly more aggressive batching for non-interactive flows; that could shave 10-15% off. But for interactive flows we keep conservative numbers to hit P95/P99 SLOs.
00:02:34 - Priya Raman: Can you quantify effect on P99 if we enable prefix KV cache and move some inference to quantized variants?
00:02:41 - Diego Alvarez: From prior pilots, prefix caching can improve P99 by ~80-120ms depending on cache hit-rates. Quantized model variants reduce token compute and can tighten median latency, but sometimes add variance on first token for certain kernels. For your workload I'd expect net P99 improvement of 70-150ms if you adopt both. We'll verify with a run on your sample.
00:03:02 - Jules Martin: Important for us is predictable tail latency — so even if median is good, P99 is what product owners look at. Also need to confirm encryption-at-rest in EU and key management.

00:03:14 - Maya Chen: On security, we support customer-managed keys via KMS and can keep audit logs retained per region. We also have SOC 2 Type II; our compliance docs are in the security packet we'll share.
00:03:25 - Liam O'Rourke: When is your next SOC 2 audit window? We need to line that up with our vendor review.
00:03:30 - Diego Alvarez: We completed Type II in Q2 2026; next recertification schedule is being finalized but we'll give you the latest attestation now. I'll include the letter in the follow-up.

00:03:40 - Priya Raman: For the EU onramp, legal insists on VPC peering — private plane — and logs not leaving EU. Can Redwood provision a private control plane?
00:03:51 - Diego Alvarez: Yes, for Private customers we can provide a private control plane that sits in your VPC or a customer-managed VPC peering. For hosted Dedicated we can also confine data residency to EU regions and we support per-tenant audit logs retained in-region. The main difference is support SLA and network egress control.
00:04:11 - Jules Martin: Cost delta? Private control plane + on-prem style options usually bump the platform fee.
00:04:17 - Maya Chen: Correct. We'll put the platform fee delta in the pricing spreadsheet. For many customers the tradeoff is worth it for compliance.

00:04:28 - Liam O'Rourke: About APAC — we don't want full EU-on-prem style commitment, but we might pilot APAC burst during a marketing campaign in late Jan. What's the quickest path to do a short-lived APAC burst without long term capacity there?
00:04:41 - Diego Alvarez: You can use burst capacity routed to APAC region with multi-region fallback. For short pilots we can provision a temporary pool (30–60 days) with minimal platform changes — but to minimize cold-start latency you'll want a warm cache in the APAC region; that means we pre-stage KV states for your most common prefixes. There's a small setup fee and warm-up window.
00:05:04 - Priya Raman: What's the warm-up time roughly?
00:05:07 - Diego Alvarez: Depends on model and token history; usually 24–72 hours if we pre-seed with representative requests. If you can't pre-seed we'll see higher first-token variance for the first day.
00:05:18 - Liam O'Rourke: Okay. Timeline: renewal mid-December, we want EU pilot in December (two-week), APAC pilot end of January. Is that feasible?
00:05:28 - Diego Alvarez: EU pilot in December is feasible but will require paperwork and VPC setup this month, so quick turnaround on security questionnaire and a PO helps. APAC in late Jan is fine — we'll schedule warm-up a week prior.

00:05:40 - Maya Chen: I'm going to walk through three contract options then: 12-month commit with moderate uplift and burst credits, 24-month commit with a discount and capacity headroom, and a short-term 3-month add-on for APAC pilot. We'll attach SOW language for VPC and data residency.
00:05:56 - Jules Martin: For discounts — are they tied to committed tokens or committed RPS? We prefer RPS because our usage is spiky.
00:06:03 - Maya Chen: We can structure commits either by sustained throughput (reserved GPUs / capacity units) or by committed spend. For spiky workloads committing to baseline RPS plus burst credits often maps better. We'll show both mapping examples.

00:06:18 - Liam O'Rourke: On the technical side, Diego, can you confirm that you can run our regression prompt suite during benchmarking? We need to make sure generation quality doesn't regress on quantized models.
00:06:28 - Diego Alvarez: Absolutely. We'll run your eval harness and include Rouge/BLEU-like metrics and hallucination checks. If quantization drops quality beyond your thresholds we won't recommend production rollout.
00:06:40 - Priya Raman: What about routing policy — we want eu traffic to always stay in eu, otherwise fall back to nearest region. Is that supported?
00:06:46 - Diego Alvarez: Yes, routing policies can be pinned by customer route; we can set hard-geo rules so that requests with EU-namespace get routed only to EU-enabled pools. Fallback policies can be set to fail-open or failover to alternate within the same legal boundary.
00:07:00 - Jules Martin: Slight aside — do you provide request-level tracing? We need to tie traces back to our APM.
00:07:06 - Maya Chen: We support trace IDs in responses and can push logs to your logging endpoint; Diego will follow up with integration patterns for Datadog/NewRelic.

00:07:16 - Liam O'Rourke: Ok. Pricing sensitivity — if we go 24-month, what's the max discount on platform fee and per-token rate?
00:07:24 - Maya Chen: Without getting into exact numbers on the call, 24-months typically gets up to an additional 10–15% off baseline unit rates and reduced platform fee. Exact depends on commit size. I'll send a model with breakpoints.

00:07:38 - Priya Raman: Any hidden costs we should worry about? Egress or unexpected charge lines?
00:07:42 - Diego Alvarez: Egress within region is minimal; cross-region egress is billed per GB. Private control plane options include a one-time provisioning fee. We'll surface those clearly in the sheet.

00:07:52 - Maya Chen: Quick check — you mentioned P99 spikes to 700ms. If we provision baseline in EU and enable prefix caching + light quantization, we expect that to drop into the 300–450ms range at P99. Diego will run the benchmark to validate.
00:08:07 - Diego Alvarez: Yes, we'll include P50/P95/P99 and also tail percentile histograms. We'll also show cost per 1k tokens for each config.

00:08:17 - Liam O'Rourke: Great. On SOC2 and security packet — we need the attestations and a completed security questionnaire by next week ideally.
00:08:25 - Maya Chen: Noted, we'll attach SOC2 and the security packet in the follow-up email.

00:08:30 - Priya Raman: For the EU VPC peering, who owns the peering connection? We prefer to own it in our AWS account.
00:08:36 - Diego Alvarez: You can own the peering — we support a customer-owned peering model. We'll provide the CloudFormation templates and the runbook.

00:08:44 - Jules Martin: What about observability retention? We need 12 months of per-route latency and cost telemetry for audits.
00:08:50 - Maya Chen: We offer configurable retention — 90/365/730 days — for premium observability add-on. We'll call out the SKU in the proposal.

00:08:59 - Liam O'Rourke: One final ask: can we get a live demo of the EU onramp flow? A quick walk-through of peering, routing, and sample request path?
00:09:07 - Maya Chen: Absolutely, Diego can run a short demo — but maybe better after the benchmark when we have the actual sample. For today we'll keep to planning.

00:09:18 - Diego Alvarez: Quick note on benchmarks — to be accurate, we need a representative traffic CSV (P95, P99, seq lengths) and a few dozen sample prompts. Priya, you mentioned sharing that?
00:09:28 - Priya Raman: Yes, I'll export last month's traffic slice and include the prompt list, redacted as needed. Aim to send that by Wednesday.

00:09:36 - Liam O'Rourke: We'll also loop in procurement. Jules will own contract term decision but wants options.
00:09:42 - Jules Martin: Yep. Procurement will push back on platform fee increases but we can justify with compliance needs.

00:09:50 - Maya Chen: Great. I'll summarize next steps: Redwood runs benchmarks, sends pricing, shares SOC2 & security packet, and we sketch the EU two-week pilot SOW. We aim to reconvene after benchmarks.

00:10:05 - Liam O'Rourke: Sounds good. Any open questions from BlueOak?
00:10:09 - Priya Raman: Minor point — do you support SAML SSO for console access for our operators?
00:10:14 - Diego Alvarez: Yes, SAML/SCIM provisioning are supported. We'll include the SSO setup doc.

00:10:20 - Maya Chen: I'll just note action items in the recap. Diego, anything to add?
00:10:24 - Diego Alvarez: I'll run the P99 benchmark, include quantized variant numbers, and share trace integration docs.

00:10:31 - Liam O'Rourke: Perfect.

[Some sections elided — typical admin chatter, small talk, quick logistics planning]

00:38:12 - Maya Chen: Back on track — timeline check. If BlueOak can send the sample traffic by 2026-11-04 and sign a short PO to start the pilot infra, we can get the EU pilot running the week of 2026-11-29 and finish the two-week pilot before the mid-December renewal.
00:38:30 - Priya Raman: That timeline works if legal moves quickly. We'll aim to get the questionnaire back in 72 hours.
00:38:37 - Jules Martin: Procurement needs two weeks for an internal review, but we can issue a PO with a provisional SOW.
00:38:44 - Diego Alvarez: For the APAC pilot we'll schedule warm-up the week before your campaign and require ~48 hours for cache pre-seeding once we have representative traffic.
00:38:55 - Liam O'Rourke: Okay.

00:45:01 - Maya Chen: Let's do a quick pricing sanity: if you go 12-month with 40% uplift and burst credit, rough delta is X% — I'll put exact figures in the sheet. If you go 24-month, you'll see lower unit rates. Again, details in the follow-up.
00:45:18 - Priya Raman: Please put explicit line items for private control plane and observability retention.
00:45:24 - Maya Chen: Will do.

00:46:05 - Liam O'Rourke: Last question — if we see unexpected traffic growth, what's lead time to scale baseline capacity?
00:46:12 - Diego Alvarez: For Dedicated pools we can scale in 24–48 hours depending on inventory. For Private deployments lead time is longer but we have burst bridging options so you don't hit throttles in the interim.
00:46:25 - Jules Martin: Good.

00:47:00 - Maya Chen: Alright, recap and owners: Maya will send pricing and SOW templates; Diego will run benchmarks and deliver latency + quality results; Priya will send traffic samples and questionnaire; Liam/Jules will coordinate legal/procurement. We'll meet next week to review benchmark results.
00:47:20 - Liam O'Rourke: Thanks all.
00:47:23 - Priya Raman: Thank you.
00:47:24 - Jules Martin: Thanks.
00:47:26 - Diego Alvarez: Thanks, bye.

End transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings e.g., "control plane" transcribed as "control plain" once; punctuation and speaker boundaries approximate.

Recap / Next steps (auto):

- Redwood to send pricing spreadsheet including 12/24 month models and APAC pilot SOW by 2026-11-09.
- BlueOak to send redacted traffic sample and security questionnaire by 2026-11-04.
- Schedule follow-up call week of 2026-11-09 to review benchmarks and finalize pilot PO.
